title: Quasi-coherent high cohomology of a relatively m-pseudo-coherent complex
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-morphism-conventions], let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. If $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex], then $H^i(E)$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] for every $i>m$. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, Noetherian hypothesis, or lower bound on $E$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0CSU, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, first assertion; relative m-pseudo-coherence is Definition 09UI.

proof.text: Fix $q>m$. Unpack [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] to choose affine charts $U=U_{ab}$ covering $X$, affine $V=V_a\subseteq S$, and closed immersions $i:U\hookrightarrow Y=\mathbf A^n_V$ such that $L=Ri_*(E|_U)$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. It suffices to prove quasi-coherence on each $U$: [pqf-def-coherent] is an affine-local definition. Here $H^q(E|_U)=H^q(E)|_U$: on complexes restriction discards the opens not contained in $U$, so it commutes with sheaf kernels and sheaf images and hence with their quotient defining cohomology. This works in every degree without a boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0CSU, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, proof of the first assertion

proof.text: For each such $Y,L$, [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] supplies an open cover $Y=\bigcup W_c$ and maps $P_c^\bullet\to L|_{W_c}$ from strictly perfect complexes inducing isomorphisms on $H^q$, since $q>m$. A strictly perfect complex is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-complex], taking the one-member cover and the identity model. Thus [lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent] makes $H^q(P_c^\bullet)$ quasi-coherent. The displayed isomorphisms identify these with $H^q(L)|_{W_c}$, using the restriction calculation of step 1. By the local definition [pqf-def-coherent], $H^q(L)$ is quasi-coherent on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 08E5, lemma-pseudo-coherent, proof of the high-degree assertion

proof.text: Choose a K-injective complex $J$ representing $E|_U$. By [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image], $Ri_*(E|_U)$ is represented by the termwise pushforward $i_*J$. Apply [lem-pc-closed-module-pushforward-homology] to $J^{q-1}\to J^q\to J^{q+1}$. Its canonical homology comparison gives $H^q(i_*J)\cong i_*H^q(J)$, hence $H^q(L)\cong i_*H^q(E|_U)$. This uses ordinary $\mathcal O_Y$-module direct image, as the cited homology lemma specifies; it applies to this triple inside an unbounded complex.

source.place: Tag 0CSU, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, proof of the first assertion

proof.text: Put $F=H^q(E|_U)$. Steps 2 and 3 show that $i_*F$ is quasi-coherent. Therefore $i^*i_*F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. The counit $i^*i_*F\to F$ is an isomorphism for every module $F$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-fully-faithful], so $F$ is quasi-coherent. Applying this to every chart $U_{ab}$ and using [pqf-def-coherent] proves that $H^q(E)$ is quasi-coherent on $X$. Since $q>m$ was arbitrary, this is the assertion. Only the chosen local embeddings were used; none of the additional global hypotheses excluded in the statement is needed.

source.place: Tag 0CSU, lemma-relative-pseudo-coherence, proof of the first assertion
